question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence.
Last week's rain ravaged the whole city.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. ruined.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "ravaged" means caused severe and extensive damage to; devastated or destroyed. (गंभीर क्षति पहुंचाना/तबाह करना)
◦ Example: The cyclone ravaged the coastal villages.

• Among the given options, "ruined" is the closest in meaning — it also means destroyed or spoiled beyond repair, which fits the context of rain devastating a city.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "reaffirmed" (पुनः पुष्टि करना): To state again firmly; to confirm — opposite in sense to destruction.

• Option 2: "rescinded" (रद्द करना): To cancel or revoke (usually a law, order or contract) — unrelated to physical damage.

• Option 4: "retracted" (वापस लेना): To withdraw a statement or offer previously made — also unrelated to physical destruction.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "ravage": devastate, ransack, plunder, wreck, demolish.

• Do not confuse "ravage" (to destroy) with "ravish" (to enrapture/delight, or in older usage, to seize by force) — they are commonly confused in SSC vocabulary questions.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
National development is defined as an improvement in people's daily arrangements, the provision of fundamental necessities to citizens such as food, education, social services, medical help, and so on, as well as an increase in per capita income.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. living conditions.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined phrase "daily arrangements" is vague and does not fit the context, which is about the overall standard of life of citizens — food, education, social services, medical help, and income. The most appropriate substitute is "living conditions" (जीवन स्तर/रहन-सहन की स्थितियां), which refers to the circumstances in which people live, including access to basic amenities.
◦ Example: The NGO worked to improve the living conditions of slum dwellers.

• The rest of the sentence clearly explains what is meant: "the provision of fundamental necessities... as well as an increase in per capita income" — this is a description of living conditions, not of "arrangements" in general.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "diving techniques" (गोता लगाने की तकनीकें): Refers to methods of diving underwater — completely unrelated to the context of national development.

• Option 2: "dining categories" (भोजन की श्रेणियां): Refers to types/classifications of dining — has no logical connection with development indicators.

• Option 3: "existing calamities" (मौजूदा आपदाएँ): Refers to ongoing disasters — the opposite of what is being described, since the passage speaks of improvement, not disaster.

NOTE

• In such "select the most appropriate substitute" questions, always match the underlined segment against the explanation/context given in the rest of the sentence, since the given phrase is often intentionally vague, misused, or nonsensical.

• Related phrases frequently tested: "standard of living", "quality of life", "socio-economic conditions".

question:
Select the word with the correct spelling from the options given below to fill in the blank.
They saw the beautiful ________ of the Gods in the Temples.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Idols.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Idols" — images or statues of a god or deity that are worshipped, or more generally, objects of worship or great admiration.

• Spelling key: I + D + O + L + S. There is no extra "e" after the "l" (unlike "Idoles"), and it must not be confused with "Ideals" or "Idles", which are entirely different words with different meanings.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Idoles" — incorrect spelling; an extra, non-existent "e" has been inserted before the final "s".

• Option 3: "Ideals" — a real word, but it means principles or standards worth striving for, not statues of gods; wrong word for this context.

• Option 4: "Idles" — a real word (third person singular of "to idle", meaning to spend time doing nothing), but it is completely unrelated in meaning to the context of gods in temples.

NOTE

• Do not confuse the similar-looking words idol (a worshipped image), idle (inactive) and idyll (a peaceful, picturesque scene) — all three are frequently used as distractors in SSC spelling and vocabulary questions.

• Related word: idolatry — the worship of idols.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.
The traffic sergeant proved through the test that Raj was under the influence of drugs and alcohol.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. inebriated.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "inebriated" means drunk or intoxicated, affected by alcohol or drugs to the point of impaired physical and mental control. (नशे में धुत्त)
◦ Example: The inebriated driver was unable to walk in a straight line.

• The phrase "under the influence of drugs and alcohol" is a direct definition of "inebriated" (also called "intoxicated"), which is exactly what the traffic sergeant's test proved about Raj.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "simonised" — not a standard word with a relevant meaning here (loosely derived from a car-polish brand name, "to polish"); has no connection to intoxication.

• Option 3: "ponied" — not a standard English word with a relevant meaning here; a distractor formed to resemble a real word.

• Option 4: "pocked" — means marked with pocks/pits (as in "pockmarked" skin); unrelated to intoxication.

NOTE

• Synonyms of "inebriated": intoxicated, drunk, tipsy, sloshed, plastered (informal).

• Antonym: sober.

• Options 2, 3 and 4 in this question are invented/non-standard words used purely as distractors — a common SSC technique in vocabulary-substitution questions.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
He does not buy shirts.
option_1: Shirts are not bought by him.
option_2: Shirts are not brought by him.
option_3: Shirts were not been bought by him.
option_4: Shirts were not bought by him.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Shirts are not bought by him.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "He does not buy shirts" is a negative sentence in the Simple Present Tense.

• Rule — Simple Present Tense (Negative):
◦ Active: Subject + do/does + not + V1 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + am/is/are + not + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "shirts" (plural) becomes the subject; the auxiliary for a plural subject in the present tense is "are"; the verb "buy" takes its past participle form "bought"; and "he" becomes the agent "by him".
◦ Passive: Shirts are not bought by him.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 is incorrect because "brought" is the past participle of "bring", not of "buy" — a common spelling/word-confusion trap.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "were not been bought" is grammatically wrong — it wrongly combines the past tense auxiliary "were" with "been", producing a non-existent verb form.

• Option 4 is incorrect because "were not bought" is the passive form of the Simple Past Tense ("He did not buy shirts"), not of the Simple Present Tense used in the original sentence.

NOTE

• Do not confuse the past participles "bought" (from buy) and "brought" (from bring) — this is one of the most common SSC distractor pairs.

• The tense of the passive sentence must always match the tense of the active sentence.

question: Identify the sentence that correctly uses the indefinite article.
option_1: She purchased a apple in the market with me.
option_2: She purchased an apple in the market with me.
option_3: She purchased apple in the market with me.
option_4: She purchase a apple in the market with me.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. She purchased an apple in the market with me.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rule — Indefinite Article "a/an": "an" is used before words that begin with a vowel sound (a, e, i, o, u), while "a" is used before words beginning with a consonant sound.

• The word "apple" begins with the vowel sound /æ/, so it must be preceded by "an", not "a".

• The sentence must also be grammatically complete and use the correct verb tense: "purchased" (past tense) correctly matches the past time frame described.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "a apple" wrongly uses "a" before a vowel sound; it should be "an apple".

• Option 3 is incorrect because the article is missing altogether before "apple" — a countable singular noun must always take an article.

• Option 4 is incorrect for two reasons: it uses "a apple" instead of "an apple", and it wrongly uses the base form "purchase" instead of the past tense "purchased".

NOTE

• The choice between "a" and "an" depends on the sound, not the spelling, of the following word — e.g., "an hour" (silent h) but "a university" (sounds like "yoo-").

• Common SSC traps: "an honest man", "a European", "an MBA", "a one-rupee coin".

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
She is building a new house.
option_1: A new house is being built by her.
option_2: She had built a new house.
option_3: She has built a new house.
option_4: A new house has been built by her.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. A new house is being built by her.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "She is building a new house" is in the Present Continuous Tense.

• Rule — Present Continuous Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + is/am/are + V1+ing + Object
◦ Passive: Object + is/am/are + being + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "a new house" becomes the subject; the subject "she" is third person singular, so the auxiliary is "is"; "being" is inserted; and "build" takes its past participle form "built".
◦ Passive: A new house is being built by her.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 is incorrect because "had built" is the active form of the Past Perfect Tense, and it has not even been converted to the passive voice.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "has built" is the active form of the Present Perfect Tense, not the Present Continuous Tense of the original sentence, and it is also not in passive voice.

• Option 4 is incorrect because "has been built" is the passive form of the Present Perfect Tense ("She has built a new house"), not of the Present Continuous Tense.

NOTE

• The structural marker "being" is unique to the passive of continuous tenses (is/am/are/was/were + being + V3); its presence or absence is a key clue in such questions.

• Passive voice of the Present/Past Perfect Continuous tenses is generally avoided/considered awkward in standard English and is rarely tested.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.
The company was engaged in spurious trade practices.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Fraudulent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "spurious" means not genuine, authentic or true; fake, counterfeit, or based on deception. (जाली/धोखाधड़ी वाला)
◦ Example: The market was flooded with spurious medicines.

• "Fraudulent" means obtained, done by, or involving deception, especially criminal deception, which closely matches the meaning of "spurious" in the context of dishonest trade practices.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Effective" (प्रभावी): Means successful in producing the desired result — opposite in sense; not related to dishonesty.

• Option 3: "Spacious" (विशाल): Means having ample space or room — completely unrelated in meaning.

• Option 4: "Trendy" (फैशनेबल): Means fashionable or currently popular — unrelated to genuineness or honesty.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "spurious": bogus, counterfeit, fake, sham, phoney.

• Antonyms of "spurious": genuine, authentic, legitimate, bona fide.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Intriguing
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Interesting.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "intriguing" means arousing one's curiosity or interest; fascinating. (दिलचस्प/जिज्ञासा जगाने वाला)
◦ Example: She told an intriguing story about her travels.

• Among the options, "interesting" is the closest and most general synonym, capturing the sense of something that captures one's attention and curiosity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Glorifying" (महिमामंडित करना): Means praising highly or making something seem more admirable than it is — a different sense (praise, not curiosity).

• Option 2: "Ravishing" (मनोहर): Means extremely beautiful or delightful, usually of physical appearance — a different quality (beauty, not curiosity).

• Option 3: "Stunning" (चकाचौंध करने वाला): Means extremely impressive or attractive, often due to beauty — again about impressiveness/beauty, not curiosity.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "intriguing": fascinating, engrossing, absorbing, captivating.

• Do not confuse "intriguing" (arousing curiosity) with words describing beauty (ravishing, stunning) — SSC frequently places both types of options together as distractors.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.
Sajni had / interfere in / this matter.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. interfere in.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence begins with "Sajni had", which requires a verb in its third form (V3) to complete the Past Perfect Tense.

• Rule — Past Perfect Tense: Subject + had + V3 + Object.

• The given part "interfere in" uses the base form (V1) of the verb instead of the past participle "interfered in", which makes it grammatically incorrect after "had".
◦ Correct sentence: Sajni had interfered in this matter.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "No error" is incorrect because there is in fact a verb-form error in the sentence, as explained above.

• Option 3: "this matter" is incorrect because this part is grammatically correct as the object of the sentence; it needs no change.

• Option 4: "Sajni had" is incorrect because this part correctly sets up the Past Perfect auxiliary "had"; the error lies in the verb that follows it, not here.

NOTE

• After the auxiliary "had", the verb must always be in its past participle (V3) form, e.g., had gone, had eaten, had interfered.

• The verb "interfere" takes the preposition "in" (interfere in a matter) or "with" (interfere with someone's work) — both are correct depending on context.

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below. While the first and the last sentences (S1 and S6) are in the correct order, the sentences in between are jumbled up and named P, Q, R, S. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

(S1) Today, the world has become a much smaller place, thanks to the adventures and miracles of science.
(P) We are slowly realising that the world is a single cooperative group.
(Q) Other religions have become forces with which we have to reckon, and we are seeking for ways and means by which we can live together in peace and harmony.
(R) Mingling of population is bringing about interchange of thought.
(S) Foreign nations have become our next-door neighbours.
(S6) We cannot have religious unity and peace so long as we assert that we are in possession of the light and all others are groping in the darkness.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. S, R, P, Q.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Read the fixed sentences first: S1 states that the world has become smaller due to science, and S6 concludes that religious unity is impossible while people believe only they possess "the light".

• S logically follows S1 — "the world has become smaller" is directly explained by "foreign nations have become our next-door neighbours."

• R follows S — the neighbouring of foreign nations ("mingling of population") leads to "interchange of thought."

• P follows R — this interchange of thought is what makes "we are slowly realising that the world is a single cooperative group."

• Q follows P and leads into S6 — since the world is a cooperative group, "other religions have become forces with which we have to reckon", and we seek peace and harmony — which sets up S6's point about the need for religious unity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 (S, R, P, Q).

Additional Information

• Option 2 (P, Q, R, S) is incorrect because it starts with "we are slowly realising..." (P), which is a conclusion drawn from earlier reasoning (S and R) that has not yet been presented — this breaks the logical cause-and-effect chain.

• Option 3 (S, R, Q, P) is incorrect because it places Q ("other religions have become forces...") before P ("we are slowly realising..."), reversing the logical order in which the general realisation (P) should lead into the specific point about religion and peace (Q), which then connects to S6.

• Option 4 (Q, R, S, P) is incorrect because it begins with Q, which refers to "other religions" — a specific idea that has no connection yet to S1's point about the world becoming smaller through science; the paragraph would make no logical sense starting this way.

NOTE

• In para-jumble questions, always identify pronoun/idea links first (e.g., what does "this" or "such" refer to) and look for cause-effect or general-to-specific chains.

• Here, the chain is: smaller world (S1) → close neighbours (S) → interchange of thought (R) → cooperative-group realisation (P) → tolerance of other religions (Q) → conclusion on religious unity (S6).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Bad iron
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Bad luck.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Bad iron" is used to mean bad luck or misfortune. (दुर्भाग्य)
◦ Example: Losing his job the same week his car broke down — that was really bad iron for him.

• In such idiom-meaning questions, the idiom is tested as a fixed expression and must be matched to its listed conventional meaning rather than interpreted literally, since "iron" here does not refer to the metal or the appliance at all.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "No steam" would relate to a literal, unrelated reading involving an iron (the appliance) having no steam — not the idiomatic sense tested here.

• Option 2: "Not hot" is again a literal reading connected to a heated iron, and has nothing to do with the idiomatic meaning of misfortune.

• Option 4: "Bad behaviour" describes conduct or manners, which is unrelated to the sense of ill fortune conveyed by the idiom.

NOTE

• Other idioms/phrases expressing luck frequently tested in SSC: "a stroke of luck" (a lucky event), "down on one's luck" (experiencing a period of bad luck), "as luck would have it" (by chance).

• Idiom-based questions must be answered from the fixed, listed meaning of the expression, not from a literal word-by-word translation.

question: Select the sentence that contains no spelling errors.
option_1: The mall road of our city is always teyming with street vendors.
option_2: The mall road of our city is always tiiming with street vendors.
option_3: The mall road of our city is always tyming with street vendors.
option_4: The mall road of our city is always teeming with street vendors.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The mall road of our city is always teeming with street vendors.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "teeming" — the present participle of "teem", meaning to be full of, crowded, or swarming with something.

• Spelling key: T + double E + M + ING. The double "e" (as in "teem") must be retained, and no extra or substituted vowels should be added.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "teyming" — incorrect; the letter "y" has wrongly replaced the second "e".

• Option 2: "tiiming" — incorrect; "ii" has wrongly replaced "ee", and this misspells the word entirely.

• Option 3: "tyming" — incorrect; the double "e" has been dropped and replaced with a single "y", producing a non-word.

NOTE

• The verb "to teem" means to be full of or crowded with (e.g., "the river teems with fish"); it should not be confused with "team" (a group working together), which is a homophone-like word often confused in spelling questions.

• Other commonly tested double-"e" spellings: agreement, freedom, between, degree.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence.
I always enjoy the company of respectful teachers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. dutiful.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "respectful" means showing proper regard, courtesy, and deference towards others, and conscientiously fulfilling what is due to them. (आदरपूर्ण/कर्तव्यनिष्ठ)
◦ Example: A dutiful and respectful teacher always treats students and colleagues with courtesy.

• Among the given options, "dutiful" (conscientiously performing one's duties and obligations towards others, including showing them proper regard) is the closest fit, since both words involve conscientiously observing what is proper and owed to others.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "admiring" (प्रशंसात्मक): Means feeling or expressing wonder and approval — a related but distinct feeling of esteem, not the same as showing courteous regard.

• Option 2: "derogatory" (अपमानजनक): Means showing disrespect or criticism — an antonym of "respectful", not a synonym.

• Option 4: "insolent" (धृष्ट): Means rude and disrespectful, showing a lack of proper regard — also an antonym of "respectful".

NOTE

• Since two of the four options (derogatory, insolent) are clear antonyms of the given word, always eliminate opposite-meaning options first in synonym questions.

• Related words: deferential, courteous, considerate are other common synonyms of "respectful" tested by SSC.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
A sentimental memory of the past
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Nostalgia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Nostalgia" means a sentimental longing or wistful affection for a period, place, or experience in the past. (बीते समय की याद)
◦ Example: Looking at old photographs filled her with nostalgia for her childhood.

• This word precisely matches the given phrase "a sentimental memory of the past", as it specifically denotes an emotional, wistful recollection of earlier times.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Hysteria" (उन्माद): An exaggerated or uncontrollable emotional reaction, often of fear or excitement — unrelated to memories of the past.

• Option 3: "Mania" (उन्माद): An excessive enthusiasm or obsessive desire for something — not connected to sentimental memory.

• Option 4: "Euphoria" (परम आनंद): A feeling of intense excitement and happiness in the present moment — unrelated to reminiscence of the past.

NOTE

• Related word: "nostalgic" (adjective) — feeling or expressing nostalgia.

• Other one-word substitutes frequently tested with "memory/past": reminiscence (the enjoyable recollection of past events), retrospect (a survey or review of a past course of events).

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom or phrase to fill in the blank in the given sentence.
Sweety has been ________ since her painting won first prize.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. walking on air.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "walking on air" means feeling extremely happy or elated. (बेहद खुश होना)
◦ Example: Ever since he got the promotion, he has been walking on air.

• Since Sweety's painting won first prize, she would naturally be extremely happy — exactly the sense conveyed by "walking on air".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "walking on eggshells" (बहुत सावधानी से व्यवहार करना): Means behaving very cautiously so as not to upset or offend someone — unrelated to the joy of winning a prize.

• Option 2: "waiting in the wings": Means being ready and prepared to take on a role or opportunity when it arises — does not fit the context of celebrating a win.

• Option 3: "walking into the lion's den": Means entering a dangerous or hostile situation — the opposite of a happy, celebratory context.

NOTE

• Other idioms expressing extreme happiness: "on cloud nine", "over the moon", "in seventh heaven", "jump for joy".

• Idioms with "walking" are frequently tested together as a set (walking on eggshells, walking on air, walking on thin ice) — note the differing meanings carefully.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.
He became ________ (verbose) after a few drinks.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. talkative.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "verbose" means using or containing more words than necessary; excessively wordy or talkative. (बहुत बोलने वाला)
◦ Example: After a few drinks, he became verbose and would not stop talking.

• "Talkative" (inclined to talk a great deal) is the closest and most natural synonym of "verbose" in this context, matching the sense of someone speaking excessively.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "aggressive" (आक्रामक): Means ready or likely to attack or confront — relates to hostility, not excessive talking.

• Option 2: "decisive" (निर्णायक): Means able to make decisions quickly and firmly — unrelated to wordiness.

• Option 3: "exhaustive" (विस्तृत): Means covering all aspects thoroughly and in detail (usually of a study/list) — close in the sense of "detailed" but not used to describe a person's manner of speaking the way "verbose"/"talkative" is.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "verbose": wordy, long-winded, garrulous, loquacious.

• Antonym: "terse" or "succinct" (brief and to the point).

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
A large number of fish swimming together
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Shoal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Shoal" is the collective noun/one-word substitute for a large number of fish swimming together. (मछलियों का झुंड)
◦ Example: A shoal of sardines swam past the divers.

• This is a fixed collective noun tested frequently in SSC one-word substitution questions, similar to "flock" (birds/sheep) or "herd" (cattle).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Stream" (धारा): Refers to a small, narrow river or a continuous flow of something — not a collective noun for fish.

• Option 3: "Sheaf" (पूला/गट्ठर): Refers to a bundle of things tied together, especially grain stalks or papers — unrelated to fish.

• Option 4: "String" (माला/लड़ी): Refers to a series of similar items or events, or a thin cord — not the standard term for a group of fish.

NOTE

• Other collective nouns frequently tested by SSC: a swarm of bees, a pride of lions, a pack of wolves, a flock of birds/sheep, a herd of cattle/elephants, a school of dolphins/whales (also used for fish alongside "shoal").

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Eloquent
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Impotent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Eloquent" means fluent and persuasive in speaking or writing; having or exerting the power of forceful, effective expression. (धाराप्रवाह/प्रभावशाली वाणी वाला)
◦ Example: She gave an eloquent speech that moved the entire audience.

• "Impotent" means lacking power, strength, or effectiveness; powerless. Since "eloquent" is fundamentally about having the power to move and persuade through speech, "impotent" (lacking that power) is treated as its antonym in this pair — an eloquent speaker has forceful, effective expression, while an impotent one is powerless to express or persuade.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Modest" (विनम्र): Means having or showing a moderate estimation of one's own qualities; unassuming — describes personality/humility, not speaking ability.

• Option 2: "Crucial" (महत्वपूर्ण): Means extremely important or decisive — unrelated to the quality of speech.

• Option 4: "Humble" (विनम्र): Means having a modest or low estimate of one's own importance — again a personality trait, not the opposite of fluent/persuasive speech.

NOTE

• Synonyms of "eloquent": fluent, articulate, expressive, persuasive.

• Other antonyms sometimes accepted for "eloquent" in general usage: inarticulate, tongue-tied, halting — but among the options given here, "impotent" (powerless) is the intended antonym, based on the sense of "eloquent" as having forceful, persuasive power.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.
As cattle are to herd so are birds to ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. flock.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• This is an analogy based on collective nouns. Just as a group of cattle is called a "herd", a group of birds is called a "flock". (पक्षियों का झुंड)
◦ Example: A flock of pigeons flew over the rooftops.

• The relationship to be completed is: cattle : herd :: birds : flock.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "litter": Is the collective term for a group of animals born to the same mother at one time (e.g., a litter of puppies/kittens), not for birds.

• Option 3: "pack": Is the collective term for wolves, dogs, or a group of hunting animals, not for birds.

• Option 4: "streak": Is used as the collective noun for tigers, not for birds.

NOTE

• Common collective-noun analogies tested by SSC: cattle – herd, birds – flock, wolves – pack, lions – pride, fish – shoal/school, puppies/kittens – litter, tigers – streak/ambush.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

All state universities and colleges in Uttar Pradesh, one of the (1)________ in India, will now (2)________ a “save water” ritual named ‘Jal Bharo’ in place of ‘lamp lighting’ to inaugurate their annual convocations. The governor of the state, who is also chancellor of state universities, instructed that every university and college in the state should install rainwater harvesting plants on its campus. ‘Jal Bharo’ signifies (3)________ the vision of ‘Jal Shakti’. This ceremony symbolises the (4)________ importance of water conservation, whereas the lamp lighting ceremony symbolised removing darkness through education and spreading the light of learning. It is really a (5)________ initiative. Every educational institute in India should ensure to save and recharge groundwater by installing rainwater harvesting plants. These kinds of initiatives provide awareness of using and saving water, the elixir of life.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. biggest states.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "All state universities and colleges in Uttar Pradesh, one of the (1)________ in India..." The phrase **"one of the ________" must be followed by a plural noun in the superlative degree**, since it describes Uttar Pradesh as being among the top-ranking group of states in the whole of India.

• Rule — "one of the + superlative adjective + plural noun": This fixed structure is used to say that something belongs to the top group of its kind, e.g., "one of the tallest buildings", "one of the richest countries". Here, "biggest states" correctly completes this structure, referring to Uttar Pradesh being one of the largest states (by area/population) in India.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "more big states" is incorrect because "more big" is not a valid comparative/superlative form; the correct superlative of "big" is "biggest", not "more big".

• Option 2: "big state" is incorrect because it is singular and uses the positive degree ("big"), not the superlative required after "one of the", and it does not agree grammatically with "the".

• Option 4: "bigger state" is incorrect because "bigger" is the comparative degree (used to compare two things), whereas "one of the ________" always requires the superlative degree ("biggest") along with a plural noun.

NOTE

• The structure "one of the + superlative + plural noun" is a very common SSC grammar point — remember that a singular noun after "one of the superlative" is always incorrect (e.g., "one of the best players" is correct, not "one of the best player").

• Degrees of comparison: big – bigger – biggest (positive – comparative – superlative).

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

All state universities and colleges in Uttar Pradesh, one of the (1)________ in India, will now (2)________ a “save water” ritual named ‘Jal Bharo’ in place of ‘lamp lighting’ to inaugurate their annual convocations. The governor of the state, who is also chancellor of state universities, instructed that every university and college in the state should install rainwater harvesting plants on its campus. ‘Jal Bharo’ signifies (3)________ the vision of ‘Jal Shakti’. This ceremony symbolises the (4)________ importance of water conservation, whereas the lamp lighting ceremony symbolised removing darkness through education and spreading the light of learning. It is really a (5)________ initiative. Every educational institute in India should ensure to save and recharge groundwater by installing rainwater harvesting plants. These kinds of initiatives provide awareness of using and saving water, the elixir of life.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. organise.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "...will now (2)________ a ‘save water’ ritual named ‘Jal Bharo’..." The modal auxiliary "will" has already been used, and after "will", the verb must be in its base form (V1), since the sentence is in the Simple Future Tense.

• Rule — Simple Future Tense: Subject + will/shall + V1 + Object. No "-ing" form or perfect form can follow "will" directly.

• Applying the rule: "will now (2)________" must take the base form "organise", giving "will now organise a 'save water' ritual".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "organising" is incorrect because the "-ing" form cannot directly follow the modal "will" without an auxiliary like "be" (e.g., "will be organising" would be valid, but "will organising" is not).

• Option 3: "have managed" is incorrect because this is a present perfect form, which cannot follow the modal "will" directly in this construction, and it also changes the intended meaning (organising the ritual, not managing it).

• Option 4: "managing" is incorrect for the same reason as Option 2 — an "-ing" form cannot directly follow "will" — and "managing" is also not the most contextually appropriate verb compared to "organise".

NOTE

• After modal auxiliaries (will, shall, can, may, must, should, would, could, might), the main verb is always used in its base form (V1).

• To use a continuous sense with a modal, "be" must be inserted: will + be + V1+ing (e.g., "will be organising").

The governor of the state, who is also chancellor of state universities, instructed that every university and college in the state should install rainwater harvesting plants on its campus. ‘Jal Bharo’ signifies (3)________ the vision of ‘Jal Shakti’. This ceremony symbolises the (4)________ importance of water conservation, whereas the lamp lighting ceremony symbolised removing darkness through education and spreading the light of learning. It is really a (5)________ initiative. Every educational institute in India should ensure to save and recharge groundwater by installing rainwater harvesting plants. These kinds of initiatives provide awareness of using and saving water, the elixir of life.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. strengthening.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "‘Jal Bharo’ signifies (3)________ the vision of ‘Jal Shakti’." The passage is about promoting water conservation, and the ritual 'Jal Bharo' is described as symbolically reinforcing the government's water-conservation mission ('Jal Shakti').

• "Strengthening" fits best contextually, meaning making the vision of Jal Shakti stronger, more firmly established, or reinforced through this new ritual, which is consistent with the overall theme of the passage (spreading awareness and commitment towards water conservation).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "holding" does not fit naturally with "the vision" — one does not typically say a ritual "signifies holding a vision" in this context.

• Option 2: "proceeding" does not collocate meaningfully with "the vision" either; "proceeding the vision" is not idiomatic English.

• Option 3: "moving" is vague here and does not convey the intended sense of the ritual actively reinforcing or promoting the government's water-conservation vision as clearly as "strengthening" does.

NOTE

• In cloze passages, always select the option that best fits both the grammar and the overall theme/tone of the passage — here, the theme is the importance and promotion of water conservation, so a word implying reinforcement/emphasis ("strengthening") fits best.

• Common collocations with "vision": "strengthening a vision", "realising a vision", "pursuing a vision", "sharing a vision".

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. immense.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "This ceremony symbolises the (4)________ importance of water conservation..." The blank requires an adjective that naturally collocates with "importance" to emphasise how great or significant water conservation is.

• "Immense importance" is a natural and commonly used collocation in English, meaning very great or exceptionally significant importance, which fits the context of emphasising the critical need for water conservation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "sheer" typically collocates with words like "sheer size", "sheer volume", or "sheer determination" to mean "nothing but" or "complete" in an emphatic sense, but "sheer importance" is not a natural or standard collocation.

• Option 2: "complete" does not collocate naturally with "importance" either — "complete importance" is an awkward, non-idiomatic phrase in standard English.

• Option 4: "total" similarly does not pair naturally with "importance" — "total importance" is not a standard collocation, unlike "immense importance".

NOTE

• Cloze passage questions often test collocations (words that naturally go together) rather than pure grammar — "immense importance", "vital importance", and "great importance" are all standard, frequently used phrases.

• Other words that commonly collocate with "importance": utmost, paramount, considerable, growing.

solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. laudable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "It is really a (5)________ initiative." The passage praises the 'Jal Bharo' ritual as a positive step towards water conservation, so the blank requires an adjective meaning praiseworthy or commendable.

• "Laudable" means deserving praise and commendation, which fits perfectly with the passage's overall positive, appreciative tone towards this water-saving initiative.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "louder" is a comparative adjective relating to sound/volume — completely irrelevant to describing an "initiative".

• Option 3: "labelled" means given a name or classification — it does not convey the evaluative, appreciative sense required by the context, and does not fit grammatically or logically as a description of the initiative's worth.

• Option 4: "lower" is a comparative adjective meaning less in position/degree — unrelated to describing the merit of an initiative, and contradicts the passage's positive tone.

NOTE

• Words describing praiseworthy actions/initiatives frequently tested by SSC: commendable, praiseworthy, admirable, laudable, meritorious.

• Always check that the chosen word matches both the grammatical slot (here, an adjective before "initiative") and the overall tone of the passage (here, clearly positive/appreciative).
